Class RainbowGumLogManager

java.lang.Object
java.util.logging.LogManager
io.jstach.rainbowgum.jul.logmanager.RainbowGumLogManager
public final class RainbowGumLogManager extends LogManager
A LogManager implementation that vends RainbowGumJULLoggers, routing every java.util.logging.Logger call directly through Rainbow Gum instead of the normal Handler/Level dispatch. Modeled closely on org.apache.logging.log4j.jul.LogManager (log4j-jul), including its guard against reentrant getLogger(String) calls.

Installation is a JVM-wide, one-shot decision made before this class is even loaded. Set the system property java.util.logging.manager to this class's fully qualified name, as a real -D JVM argument (or via JDK_JAVA_OPTIONS), before any code in the JVM touches java.util.logging: 

java.util.logging.manager=io.jstach.rainbowgum.jul.logmanager.RainbowGumLogManager
LogManager.getLogManager() resolves this property exactly once, via a static bootstrap, so calling System.setProperty(String, String) after the JVM has started is too late; see this class's own package for why that forces this module's own tests into dedicated, non-reused-fork JVMs.

GraalVM native image: this module bundles a native-image.properties (at META-INF/native-image/io.jstach.rainbowgum/rainbowgum-jul-logmanager/) with -Djava.util.logging.manager=... plus a matching --initialize-at-build-time=io.jstach.rainbowgum.jul.logmanager.RainbowGumLogManager as native-image build arguments - the same technique Helidon's own helidon-logging-log4j module uses for its equivalent LogManager. Baking the property into the build lets LogManager's static bootstrap run once, during the build itself in a real JDK environment, so the fully-initialized RainbowGumLogManager instance ends up frozen directly into the image heap with nothing left to resolve at startup - verified with a real GraalVM build, the resulting executable needs no runtime argument at all, not even the -D above. The --initialize-at-build-time half is not optional: without it, native-image's own build-time-heap-safety analysis refuses to embed a RainbowGumLogManager instance whose type was not itself explicitly marked for build-time initialization, even though the instance was already legitimately constructed during the build.

An earlier attempt deferred java.util.logging initialization to runtime instead (--initialize-at-run-time=java.util.logging) so the system property above could be passed at native-image runtime exactly like on a normal JVM - that works, but costs two runtime -D arguments instead of zero: a native-image executable has no JDK installation directory behind it, and LogManager's primordial-configuration-file lookup throws Error: Can't find java.home ?? unconditionally once it actually runs at startup, regardless of whether a custom LogManager is even in play - -Djava.home= anything non-null would also have been required alongside the property above, for every consumer, forever. Baking the property into the build avoids that problem entirely, since the primordial-lookup code path it triggers never runs at native-image startup at all with this approach.
